Emissions in year t x ECCC SC at year t, summed in constant 2025 CAD with no further discounting across emission years. WHY THIS IS THE CENTRAL, written 3 September 2026. The two aggregations answer different questions. Each SC_t is already the present value, at year t, of the future damage stream from a tonne emitted in year t; the calendar sum therefore values each year's damage AT THE TIME IT IS CAUSED, in the money of that year held constant at 2025 prices. That is the loss-and-damage question - what harm does this buildout do, valued when it does it - and it is how Burke et al. (2026) aggregate a multi-year emissions stream. The alternative discounts each year's SC_t x E_t back to the analysis year (eccc_central_npv_2025): that is the cost-benefit question - what is the stream worth today, to weigh against benefits also expressed today - and it is how the Government of Canada's regulatory guidance aggregates a multi-year stream. The calendar sum is the central because the paper asks the loss-and-damage question. The NPV is not a sensitivity on the central; it is the right answer to the other question, and the two are carried together wherever the total is stated. NOTE: the earlier wording here - that the official schedule already embeds Ramsey discounting so a second NPV is a sensitivity only - was true of a single year's SC and did not settle the cross-year question; it is withdrawn.
